to make it short, it's an agile process where you

So we put everything that is required for the product that we
develop into the backlog and put a label to it, like must,
should, could, and won't, which is for me the most important
because that means this is out of scope.
But nevertheless, it remains in the backlog so that we can see what we are
not going to do. And then we go over this backlog again and again, and prioritize,
put the things that we are going to develop next up, and
then we translate them into these chunks that are
developable. So you have a lot of things that
you take into your sprint, and you only focus on those things for the
next three weeks. And then you have one feature developed, which you
present, get feedback, and then you go over this again.
